chunks: He sent ignominy to our foe and sent His succour to us,
till Islam got established with neck on the ground and resting in its place.
By my life, if we had also behaved like you,
no pillar of (our) religion could have been raised, nor the tree of faith could have borne leaves.
By Allah, certainly you will now milk our blood (instead of milk) and eventually you will face shame!
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of steadfastness in the establishment of Islam according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, often attributed to Imam Ali (AS) reflecting on the Battle of Badr or the Conquest of Mecca, emphasizes that divine victory (Nasr) is contingent upon sincere truthfulness (Sidq) rather than mere tactical maneuvering. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the structural integrity of Islam (the 'pillar' and 'shoot' of faith) was secured through the unwavering resolve of the early believers, contrasting their steadfastness with the eventual humiliation (Kibt) of their adversaries.
